processes.title: Third-Party with Shipping Notification
processes.memory_hook: Supplier ships direct, but we still receive a logistics signal.

sap_scope_items.label: Sales Processing Using Third-Party with Shipping Notification

processes.business_intent: Run direct supplier-to-customer fulfillment while using supplier shipping notification to update the sales-side delivery status and customer promise.

control_plane.why: creates the procurement branch instead of own-stock delivery
feeds actual shipped quantity and date back into the process
controls when customer billing becomes due

data_hinges.changes: customer-facing status and billing basis depending on design
how supplier events update the sales order
commercial settlement and potentially customer billing

impact_summary: Compared with basic TPO, the external supplier sends an explicit logistics event that improves traceability between procurement and customer order.
constraints: Notification quality becomes part of customer-service quality.
The supplier still owns physical shipment; your warehouse does not magically become involved because an ASN arrived.
lead_questions: Which supplier event updates the customer promise?
What if shipping notification and invoice quantities disagree?
Which integration message carries the notification?

processes.title: Third-Party without Shipping Notification
processes.memory_hook: Supplier ships direct; procurement and invoice events are most of what we know.

sap_scope_items.label: Sales Processing Using Third-Party without Shipping Notification

processes.business_intent: Use direct supplier-to-customer fulfillment when no supplier shipping-notification process is available or required.

control_plane.why: creates procurement from the sales item
provides expected dates when no shipping notification exists
can become the key evidence for customer billing quantity

data_hinges.changes: billing basis where invoice-related billing is used

impact_summary: The process is operationally lighter than the shipping-notification variant but has less real-time logistics evidence.
constraints: Customer visibility depends heavily on supplier confirmations and invoice timing.
Do not promise shipment visibility the integration does not actually provide.
lead_questions: What event proves the supplier shipped?
How is customer service informed before supplier invoice receipt?
Would an ASN integration materially reduce uncertainty?

processes.title: Third-Party with Variant Configuration
processes.memory_hook: Configure here, build or supply there, ship direct to the customer.

sap_scope_items.label: Sales Processing Using Third-Party with Variant Configuration

processes.business_intent: Sell a configurable product while sourcing it from an external supplier that ships directly to the customer.

control_plane.why: creates the exact product characteristic values the supplier must fulfill
keeps PO specification aligned with the customer-configured sales item
routes supply to the external vendor rather than own production or stock

data_hinges.changes: supplier specification, pricing and possibly procurement source
whether purchasing receives a valid buildable product

impact_summary: A configuration error can propagate from customer-facing sales into supplier procurement, making configuration data an integration contract rather than a UI convenience.
constraints: Supplier must be able to interpret the transferred configuration.
Changes after PO creation need explicit synchronization rules.
lead_questions: Which configuration object is authoritative after the PO exists?
How are customer changes synchronized to the supplier?
What happens if a characteristic affects both price and supplier selection?

processes.title: Make-to-Order with Variant Configuration
processes.memory_hook: The customer configuration becomes the production specification.
processes.business_intent: Create customer-specific supply where product characteristics entered in the sales order drive configuration, planning, production and costing.

control_plane.why: translates customer choices into a technically valid product
creates order-specific planning and stock
changes components, operations and commercial value

data_hinges.changes: BOM, routing, price and production specification

impact_summary: The sales order is simultaneously a commercial document and a source of production master-data context for this exact customer variant.
constraints: Configuration changes after production starts require strict change governance.
Bad dependency logic can create products that price correctly but cannot be produced, a particularly expensive form of optimism.
lead_questions: Which characteristic changes price, BOM or routing?
When is configuration frozen?
How do engineering changes affect an existing customer configuration?

processes.title: Sales Order Processing for Sales Kits
processes.memory_hook: Sell one commercial kit while logistics may execute many components.

sap_scope_items.label: Sales Order Processing for Sales Kits

processes.business_intent: Sell kit products whose BOM structure can distribute pricing and logistics relevance differently across header and components.

control_plane.why: decides price and goods-movement level
decides whether the kit can ship together
keeps commercial value aligned with physical components

impact_summary: The customer sees a product proposition; warehouse execution sees components. The model must keep those two views consistent.
constraints: Different BOM processing models change where pricing and logistics live.
Returns for kits need their own variant because components may return independently.
lead_questions: Which level owns price?
Can one component ship later?
How does a component substitution affect the commercial kit?

processes.title: Scheduling Agreement with Consignment
processes.business_intent: Combine recurring delivery schedules with consignment inventory so customer demand signals replenish and consume stock located at the customer site.

control_plane.why: drive recurring planned quantities and dates
separates physical location from ownership
triggers ownership transfer and billing

impact_summary: Two continuous controls interact: rolling demand planning and customer-located inventory ownership.
constraints: Cumulative-quantity and consignment-stock reconciliation both need reliable integration.
A schedule error can create excess stock at the customer without an immediate billing signal.
lead_questions: Is the release a replenishment forecast or a consumption signal?
How are cumulative quantities reconciled with consignment balances?
Which EDI event triggers billing?

processes.title: Just-In-Time Supply to Customer
processes.memory_hook: Forecast plans demand; the JIT call tells execution what must move now.
processes.business_intent: Execute high-frequency customer supply using JIT calls and scheduling-agreement context, typically in automotive scenarios where exact quantities, sequence and timing are operationally critical.

control_plane.why: represent the executable customer signal
provide commercial and master-data foundation
translate JIT demand into physical warehouse/shipping execution

impact_summary: The process compresses planning and execution time; an integration error becomes a physical line-side problem very quickly.
constraints: JIT requires excellent EDI/message quality and strict status handling.
Forecast and JIT signals must have clear precedence and horizon rules.
lead_questions: Which message is the legally or operationally binding signal?
How are duplicate or changed JIT calls handled?
What is the recovery design when EDI is unavailable?
